_readme: Witch tuning. Edit the numbers, push, and the playable link rebuilds. Distances are metres, times seconds, angles degrees. Keys starting with _ are notes.
_sections: The knobs come in sections (housekeeping, 2026-10-07): map, forest, witch, army, creatures, legends, party, view, light; each opens with a "__<name>" note. Within one, a note says what the knobs after it do.
__map: The map and its places: the areas, their size and shape, the beach, glades, paths, walls, scenery pieces, set pieces, the treehouse, home and the legends' clearings and relics.
_map: The forest: mapAreas x mapAreas areas cut by the fractal partition. An area is areaSize x areaScale metres across on average (areaScale 4 makes them four times as wide as the first 28 m areas; push it for bigger). areaSizeVariance (0-1) makes areas vary in size, some small, some large. borderLayers sets how wiggly borders are. Ed (2026-10-05: "make areas larger; each is effectively a fighting arena"): 14 x 14 areas of 168 m (areaScale 6), about the same world as 20 x 112 m. arena: every area is mostly open within radius metres of its centre and its soundsystem, for fights (they range 15 to 45 m), and (Ed: softer edges; then, at v473, a smaller clearing and a long soft gradient from the area's edge to near its runestone) the woods thicken over a band band metres wide beyond it, across most of the area, along curve (linear: thinning in from right past the open middle; smooth: a slow start), lone trees and bushes thinning out into the clearing, its edge wobbled by noise (a share of the band) so it's no ring; both times fight.scale. bushes and tufts: the share of the undergrowth and the ground cover left in its open middle. map.island (Ed, 2026-10-11, the journey's rosters; rules/rosters.ts, config/kinds.json): "home" plays home by roster, one area per kind she knows (the 10 kinds introduced at home and each kind whose island she's found, map.found: growing outward, its first areas the same; islandAreas its least, the kinds again past one each), its legends dealt each night, 1 in 5 areas; a kind's name (?island=fox) plays that kind's island, its own seed (where it lies on the sea chart) and size by phase (10 a phase), its roster that kind plentiful, 1-3 kinds new to its phase and the rest by bearing; empty, areas of random types as before. map.found: the kinds whose islands she's found (the night's legends favour the others).
_mapShape: The map's shape (Ed, 2026-10-06: "The map as a whole should be circular rather than square, with a buffer zone with no runestones around the edge"). islandAreas (Ed, 2026-10-11, the journey's islands: 10, the home island for now; ?island=10|20|...|64|home, ?island=off for the radius map): the island is home and exactly this many more areas, those nearest home's, round, its radius halfway out to the next (0: the radius below). shape circle: the playable areas are those whose centres lie within radius areas of home's (5.6: about 96; Ed, 2026-10-07, for about 100 areas: the best bots wake about 20 in a run, and half the creatures and trees run faster; 7.9 gave about 196, as many as the old 14 x 14), and only they get runestones, soundsystems, legends, relics and creatures and wake in waves; past them a buffer ring buffer areas deep (1 to 1.5), forest she can fly over where nothing happens; her flight's edge is the island's coast (Ed, 2026-10-11: the land map, rules/land.ts: round the borders of the playable areas, the ring of areas round them and, where it's near, the ring past that), soft over its last push metres (her speed outward easing to nothing at the edge, and a drift of up to drift m/s taking her back in); the forest goes on edge areas past it, into the fog. coast (Ed, 2026-10-06: "The island shouldn't be a totally perfect circle; make the coast slightly irregular"): which areas are playable and which the buffer's goes by their centres' distance from home over the same seeded coast, up to amp of its radius in or out (0 for a perfect circle): harmonics gentle bays and headlands (from two round the island up), plus detail (a share) of finer wobble. shape square: mapAreas x mapAreas as before (?shape=square to compare). ?mapAreas=<n> on the circular map sets the radius for about n x n areas. phase and shapes (Ed, 2026-10-11, the journey's irregular islands: rules/islandGrowth.ts): an island grows out from home over its areas' neighbours, each step the area nearest home for the island's reach that way, by its phase's shape (shapes[phase], index 0 home: near-round; 1 gently lobed; 2 bays and a peninsula; 3 arms and inlets; 4 and 5 strongly irregular): lobes, how far its outline swells and shrinks round home (a share of its reach) over harmonics bumps; arms, how far its peninsulas reach past it (a share), armCount[0] to [1] of them, each armWidth radians across; bays, how deep its bays cut in, bayCount[0] to [1] of them; jitter, each area's own seeded nudge in areas (ragged edges). Home's neighbours are always its first. phase: an island's phase when it isn't one by roster (?phase=0 to 5; a kind's island takes its own).
_lakes: Lakes (Ed, 2026-10-11, the journey's islands: rules/lakes.ts): from phase 1 some of an island's areas are water, map.shapes[phase].lakes (fewest, most) of them, each lakeSize (fewest, most) areas, never home or its neighbours, the rest of the island still joined (rules/islandGrowth.ts placeLakes); no beaches but a small shore, their water lighter than the sea; she flies over them in the treetops but never lands on the water, and on foot she and every creature stop at the shore. shore: metres of bare shore round the water (no trees, nothing placed); pad: how far from the water anything on foot stops; koi: the share of lakes with koi in them (DECISION FOR ED). biomeFrom: the island phase from which its lakes take the look of its compass biomes on the sea chart (frozen, lava, oasis, sinkhole, glacial tarn, tar pit, rust pool, lily pond; app/chartOutlines.worker.ts), before it plain water (Ed, 2026-10-12: "biome lakes can start appearing one phase earlier": 3, it was 4, the first uncharted islands). biomeFirstShare: the share of that first phase's lakes that take them, each lake seeded, the rest plain water; further out all of them, further in none (Ed, 2026-10-12: "half the lakes in the third ring are special. Further out they're all special, further in they're all plain"). The biome lakes in play (Ed, 2026-10-23: render/lakeLooks.ts, each lake the sea chart's look for it): the north's glacier's peaks kept glacierClear metres under her treetop flight (treetopHeight), and the hot springs' (the rust pools') steam: on, puffs rising rise metres over life seconds, size metres across, at opacity, a vent every spacing metres over their deep water.
_chart: The sea chart (the map table and chart.html; render/chart/seaChart.ts, render/chart/moon.ts). moon (Ed, 2026-10-12: "islands casting shadows from the moon orbiting the map screen"; #746: "have the moon rise over the North West edge of the map as you open the map screen"): each time the chart opens the moon rises over its edge at bearing from (degrees, 0 north, clockwise: -45 the north-west) over rise seconds, from just under the horizon to height degrees, then goes round once every turn seconds; every island's relief throws a shadow away from it, across the sea and into its own valleys, shadow its darkest (0 none, 1 black), the hills' shading following it; disc: its disc drawn in the sky past the rim at its bearing (hidden behind the world). edgeBand (#746: "add empty sea around the edge of the map"): the empty sea past the furthest islands, the disc's radius beyond theirs as a share of it (0 as before; at most 0.6).

chart._sailHold: Seconds the use button (E, Enter, the pad's square) or the mouse is held on an island at the map table's chart to sail there, its ring filling (Ed, 2026-10-23: "You have to hold the button to select a new island to sail to (ring fills)"); let go early, nothing. A click only chooses.

_islands: Islands other than home (the wave 2 finale's dream bubbles and the sea chart; rules/islandShape.ts, art/islands.js; Ed, docs/backlog/journey.md): coast, the coastline's knobs as map.coast's (amp, the most it strays from round, a share of the radius; harmonics, how many bays and headlands; detail, the finer wobble), stronger than home's so every island has a shape of its own, read at a bubble's 30 pixels.
_beach: The beach (Ed, 2026-10-06: "Outside of the circular map, there is the sea. A beach surrounds the island, and the calm dark water reflects the sky. You can hear the sound of the waves. If you try and fly past the beach, you land and stargaze (the party lying down pose). Other witches can be found on the beach occasionally; if you land near them, you chat, hold hands, and hug. Try and do this in a way that doesn't cost performance - most games won't ever go to the beach, it's just an Easter egg for adventurers."): sand over the last width metres inside her flight's edge (nothing grows or stands on it), the sea from shore metres past the edge, the hills eased over ease metres down to sand metres high where the sand starts and to sea metres at the water. Flying on out over the sand for restAfter seconds she lands (from the treetops too) and lies down to stargaze; any other way gets her up. Lying there facing out to sea (the north coast: the camera always looks north), the bend keeps only camera.seaward of itself, so the open water isn't dropped below a horizon of sand. Lying down, the camera stands by her bearing round the coast (Ed, 2026-10-07: "move the camera further and lower to show off the moon reflecting on the water and the beach and the sky ... check in 12 different directions for a nice composition and smoothly interpolate between them"): camera.bearings, twelve entries every 30 degrees from the north, clockwise: angle (degrees below the horizon), distance (metres back), look (metres over her it aims at), side (metres east it stands and aims: out over the water on the east and west coasts, so the shore runs up the picture with the sea beside it) and bend (the share of the stargazing bend kept there: none facing the open sea to the north, so the water isn't dropped below a horizon of sand; camera.seaward does the same on the way down to the water), joined smoothly all the way round. Lying there (Ed, 2026-10-06: "the bend shader applies so that you can see the sky") the world bends stargazeCurve times the treetops' curve (Ed: "it's stronger than usual, so the sky takes up more of the screen"), eased in and out over about gazeEase seconds, so the night sky opens up over the sea. Lying there with a beach witch (Ed: "If you land near another witch, and you stargaze together, and you wait a few seconds, little hearts will start appearing near you both, floating upwards and disappearing"): after hearts.after seconds a ❤️ rises off one or the other every hearts.every[0] to [1] seconds, for hearts.life seconds each, until either gets up; the two stay lying together until she moves. A 💌 come down on the sand or the sea (Ed: "they last longer and disappear more slowly (5 seconds)") rests letterLinger seconds, fading over the last letterFade, bobbing gently on the water. witchChance of runs (Ed, 2026-10-06: "I think there should always be beach witches, but there are only a handful spread around it": every run) have spots[0] to spots[1] spots spread round the coast (evenly, each nudged by up to a third of the gap), each with witches[0] to witches[1] witches (Ed, 2026-10-06: "Beach witches appear solo": one); landing within meet metres of them and keeping still for idleAfter seconds, one chats, holds hands, hugs and stargazes with her, turn seconds each. None of it is drawn or heard unless she's within shown metres of the sand, nor the witches stepped beyond simRange. on false: forest to the edge, as before. vary (Ed, 2026-10-06: "The beach can be more irregularly shaped"): the sand's width round the coast, width times e to the amp times a seeded smooth noise of harmonics bays and narrows; where the noise is lowest (below -rocky, of -1 to 1) it turns rocky, narrowing to rockyWidth metres; never under min. decor (Ed, 2026-10-06: "a few beach decorations, sparsely: shells, star fish, conch, footprints of people and creatures ... just nature"; rules/beachDecor.ts, art/beach.js): round the coast in sectors sectors, about finds finds a sector (shells, starfish, a conch, seaweed, pebbles; rocks on a rocky stretch), each sector with a trails chance of a trail of prints[0] to prints[1] footprints (bare feet, paws, hooves, a bird's, weighted by kinds) wandering along the sand and fading out (Ed, 2026-10-12: too many on the beach, so finds and trails halved, to 0.35 and 0.035); all of it on the wet and dry sand, the clear metres of it nearest the woods left bare. dolphins (Ed, 2026-10-07; their timetable rules/seaLife.ts, drawn by render/dolphins.ts): leaping off the east coast, within arc radians of due east, one every every[0] to [1] seconds, pair of them in twos, out[0] to [1] metres past the water's edge from her and ahead[0] to [1] metres north of that (away from the camera: the stargazing bend drops anything much more than 20 m ahead of her below the screen), each leap length metres along the coast and height high over time seconds. kraken (Ed, 2026-10-07; rules/seaLife.ts, render/kraken.ts): off the west coast, within arc radians of due west, a slot every every seconds, chance of them holding a rising: tentacles[0] to [1] tentacles rising one after another out[0] to [1] metres past the water's edge from her and ahead[0] to [1] metres north of that, each over time seconds, and in head of them the dome of its head and its eye. decor.findScale: the beach finds' size, times (Ed, 2026-10-11: twice; the footprints keep theirs). grain (Ed, 2026-10-12: "The beach is not pixelated like everything else"): how far each of the sand's art pixels is lightened or darkened at random, 0.14 = ±7%; the sand and sea draw their art pixels doubled until each covers at least a screen pixel (render/ground.ts), so the grain stays chunky under the beach's far, low camera.
_areaEdgeBlend: Blended area edges: each tree and bush takes its look (its area type) from a point up to width metres away (40: Ed, #887, 2026-10-13, so the planting blends across the borders; it was 20), the offset mostly the plant's own, drawn independently of its neighbours' (stray of it: 0.85, Ed's #887 feedback, so the kinds interleave tree by tree rather than in clumps; it was 0.5), the rest a smooth noise scale metres across so the band doesn't run dead straight; the neighbour's share ramps from about half at the border to none width metres in. Only the look: creatures, partifying and the party border keep the exact borders.
_groundBlend: How neighbouring areas' floor textures meet (Ed, v160): the border is warped by noise in two octaves (up to warp metres over about 40 m, and fine metres over about 6 m), so it meanders rather than following the texture's grid; across a band metres wide the two floors mix pixel by pixel, by noise and (dither) an ordered dither, like grass creeping into dirt. Visual only. ?blend=off turns it off.
_ground: The ground's fake relief (Ed, v171: so the ground doesn't look flat): low rises and hollows from noise about relief.scale metres across, tilting the ground's lighting by relief.strength (0 flat) so the witch's light and the campfires pick out the bumps, and hollows shaded darker by relief.shade. ?relief=0 turns it off. layout (rules/terrain.ts; Ed's idea, relayed by the coordinator 2026-10-07: runestones on high ground, legends in low, trees thicker low down): every area's runestone stands on a rise and every legend clearing lies in a hollow, rise and dip times the hills' amplitude high and deep (0.15 of 40 m: 6 m), each easing out over reach metres (kept short and low: the stones are about 110 m apart, a clearing about 65 m from its stone, and the slopes must stay under the camera's sightline) (the plateaus then level each one, so a stone tops a knoll and a clearing sits in a dell); trees grow up to trees (a share) thicker in the lowest ground and thinner on the highest, by the land's height over half the hills' amplitude (most of it lies within that). Drawing and tree placement only: the rules still move on flat ground.
_leyLines: pulseSpeed (Ed, 2026-10-09: "Pure constant speed"): the pulse's speed along the route's own curves, metres a second (1: Ed, 2026-10-18, "Default starting wave speed is 1m/s"; 4 before), times the party's tempo (a knockdown's BPM speeds it); a wave lands as it reaches the next stone, so a wave's gap is its link's length over the speed; 0 holds the pulse where it is (no waves). The boot has its own speed (boot.speed). The pause page's Waves slider sets it live, 0 to 6, remembered on this browser (config/decisions/953-waves.json, app/settings.ts); ?pulse=<m/s> or ?pulse=off sets it from a link, over the saved one. depart (Ed, 2026-10-06: "The leyline shouldn't cross the dancefloor. After going around the speaker circle it should go off to the right and loop around to whatever direction it needs to go"; it ran due south across the floor before): the first line leaves the treehouse's front round the ring of speakers, avoid metres outside it, on the first objective's side (clockwise on the screen and off to the right, the spiral starting east of home; the other way round for one west of it), then off the ring and looping round the same way out to the first objective; no link of the route passes over the dancefloor. The ley lines (Ed, 2026-10-04; 2026-10-05: "you just follow them from objective to objective"; 2026-10-06: "I think the leylines should cover the entire set of waves the whole time, but ideally it shouldn't cross itself, or try and minimise crossings"): a glowing line through every wave's runestone in the order the waves wake them, home first, the whole route the whole time (party.picker route keeps it from crossing itself): the sections ahead of the last stone reached each fade times as bright as the one before, the one just left behind behindBright times as bright as the next and each before it fade times that, none fainter than far[0] ahead or far[1] behind (as shares). brightness: how bright, a share of their first look (Ed, 2026-10-05: "about 30% as bright", 0.3), the glow through the crowns too. Each fades from the colour of the area it starts in to that of the area it ends in (the colour partified areas and soundsystems use). advance: "first" moves it on when the next area's quest is done or its wave arrives, whichever comes first; "wave" only when its wave arrives. Each wanders along the low ground between its stones, straying up to valley of its length (80 m at most) to follow the hills' valleys, and a shimmer flows along it toward the next stone at flow[0] m/s, flow[1] m apart. It stays on the ground in both modes (Ed): width metres across on the ground and over the treetops (wider there, with a faint glow through the crowns), height metres over the ground in each. reveal (Ed, 2026-10-06: "The pulse starts from the treehouse at the start of the first wave. before that, during boot up phase, there's no leyline ... Then the leyline appears, starting at the treehouse, moving three times (adjustable) the speed on the pulse (so it reaches runestone 3 by the time the first wave finishes)"): from the end of home's boot the line grows out from the treehouse along the route at this many links a wave (this many times the pulse's speed), a soft glow at its tip, reaching this stone as the first wave lands and going on at that pace until the whole route is drawn (so no stone pops on at once; rules/leypulse.ts leyReachTimes gives when it reaches each, for the beacons); none at all while home boots up. The pulse itself (render/leylines.ts) runs along the link from the last stone reached by the wave countdown's share (rules/leypulse.ts, as the HUD's wave pointer), the stretch behind it brighter, the whole link brightening toward the wave. The boot (rules/bootRing.ts): the party spell sends the pulse from the treehouse round the home ring clockwise from the top, turning each stone into its speaker, the line drawn ahead of it at reveal times its pace. ?ley=0 turns them off. Round 14 (Ed: "the leyline and pulse are not pixelated. Lighting effects can be non-pixel but they should be lighting objects that are pixels"; "the leyline is too faint"): on the ground the line is pixels, a hard core core[0] metres each side of its middle (core[1] over the treetops) in whole art pixels, a half-bright rim core[2] (core[3]) round it, its brightness worked out per art pixel along it in flat quarter steps, the pulse's head and the growing tip stepped the same way; round it the smooth glow it casts, over width; from the treetops the glow through the crowns stays smooth. brightness 0.3 -> 0.4, width [2, 4.5] -> [3, 5.5]. ?ley=0 turns them off. Its whole length (Ed, 2026-10-06: "The leyline should always go from the treehouse to 3x the progress of the pulse, and I should be able to see it along its entire length"): fade, behindBright and far all 1, so every section is as bright as the next; unbroken into and out of each stone; laid on the ground every 2 m so it never sinks into a crest; shown through the trees (never through a hill, the witch or a creature) at the same brightness; the current link as bright as the rest, the pulse only adding its head and arrival flash. advance (Ed, 2026-10-08: "The pulse should never skip, it always travels along the route at the bpm speed. The line front also never skips, but travels along the route at three times the bpm speed"): "wave" (the default) keeps the line, its pulse and its front to the waves, a quest done leaving its stone where it is on the route; "first" moves the line on to a stone as soon as its quest is done, as before (the pulse jumping to it).
_glades: The sleeping legends' clearings (Ed, 2026-10-06: "Sleeping legends should be in a small circular clearing, where they sit near the top of the circle. This magical clearing should be lit with an eerie twilight with glowing motes rising in it."; render/glades.ts): art builder 1 places them (the map's glades); until then one round each sleeping legend, radius metres across with the legend top of the way toward its top. Only those within reach metres of the witch, the nearest 4, are lit. hue, sat: the twilight's colour (a cool violet dusk, against the party's amber); light: its pool, filling the circle and soft at its edge; edge: the ring at its edge at full (a quarter of it always marks the circle), which brightens with the witch inside it or a quest sigil or relic put down in it, easing at edgeEase a second. Inside one (Ed, 2026-10-06: "When you go into the legend clearing, the rest of the forest should get darker. Maybe switch off the witch's glow when she's in there."): the forest's light and haze outside the clearing's own twilight dim by dark (0 none, 1 black), her own glow goes by glowOff (1: off; her moonlit rim stays), both eased in and out over fade seconds. motes: per to a clearing, rising rise metres a second to height metres, size art pixels, in hue and sat at bright.

wisps._: Will-o'-the-wisps in the wild areas (Ed, 2026-10-07): a seeded chance per square of ground (cell m) within reach of her; none within partyNear of a partified area, the full chance from partyFar; height [low, high] m, drift m, a cycle of period s (fade in, linger, fade out, gone); core and halo size in art pixels; colour.

_treehouse: The witch's treehouse, home (Ed, 2026-10-05: "The treehouse should be 5m due north of the dance floor, outside the speaker ring"): its footprint's nearest edge (clear metres round its foot) stands gap metres beyond the dancefloor's ring of speakers (so however many speakers or how far out, it stays outside them), at angle degrees (-90: due north, straight up the screen), always facing south, to the floor and the camera; and keeps a clearing of clear metres round its foot (at least the art's footprint: 8.2 m for the v2 tower); its lantern and fairy lights light lightReach metres round at lightStrength. The game starts with her sitting on its terrace; the first move or rise takes her off. The deck (Ed, 2026-10-11: "a circle with a wooden floor and a balustrade sitting on the ent. You land on it by being at treetop height, and during the night time slower 10x"; rules/treehouse.ts): on (false: the old treehouse), a round deck radius metres across its middle at the Ent (the treehouse's spot), its floor height metres up (Ed: "The deck sits at 22 m"); in the treetops, landing within radius + grace metres of its middle lands her on it; she walks it, kept rail metres inside its edge, round the map table in its middle (table metres round; Ed: "The world map is in the centre"; E within tableUse metres of its edge opens the sea chart) and behind the decks along its south edge (Ed: "The table holding the decks is along the curved bottom edge of the platform": decks, from where she stands behind them, inner metres out, to their front, outer, from to to degrees round, 90 due south; the Ent's art, art/ent.js, draws them there), where she starts and comes back, seat metres south of the middle. On it, landed, time runs as in a calm legend circle (legendCircle.slow). carrier (Ed, 2026-10-10, journey.md "Arriving": on a new island the Ent stands on the back of a party legend of that island's kind; drawing only, art/carrier.js): "island" that island's kind's legend, braced under the Ent, its back about 13 m up and the Ent's trunk that much shorter, so the deck stays where it is (home, the Ent's own island, has none, nor has a map that isn't an island); a kind's id (e.g. "bear", or ?carrier=bear) that kind's everywhere; "none" no one. The house (Ed, 2026-10-14, docs/backlog/treehouse.md step 1; treehouse.house, on in place of the deck; rules/treehouse.ts): the hub, a round room where the deck was (hub its radius, height its floor's, rail its wall's keep-in, table and tableUse the map's radius and reach: E there opens the chart), and the balcony hung off its south side (balcony.out its centre south of the hub's, balcony.r its radius), open at its rim either side of the decks' desk (decks, round the balcony's centre; seat her standing place behind them, from the balcony's centre): at treetop height she flies straight onto it and lands over landTime seconds, walks off its rim to fly again, or, with no broom (fall.on, a switch till the brooms are objects), falls for fall.time seconds and comes back at the magic circle (circle.out south of the hub's centre, circle.r), where a knockout brings her back too. The house's walk (Ed, 2026-10-21: "she shouldn't use her broom until she steps off the balcony"): on foot in the house (the hub, the balcony, the rooms) she walks, walk metres a second, not at her broom's groundSpeed. The dark behind the rooms (Ed, 2026-10-23: "when you're inside the treehouse in an enclosed room (i.e. not the terrace) the forest behind the tree should be black"): with dark.on, in a room or on a branch off the Terrace only the house, the Ent's crowns and her are drawn, over black; stepping onto the Terrace the forest comes back from the doorway she came through over dark.fade seconds (and goes again as she goes back in), and through the telescope it fades in over the same.
_home: Home's area (Ed, 2026-10-05: "Home area should be big enough that the whole circle, centre the dancefloor, edge the treehouse, is within it"): the map is cut with home first, a circle round the dancefloor out past the treehouse's footprint (its distance and clear) and margin metres more all home's; the areas round it are cut round it, their centres kept at least gap of an area beyond the circle.
_grounds: Old playgrounds and sports grounds (the relics art's arrangements): an area has one with chance (not home), off to the side of its centre, keeping a clearing of radius metres (per kind) where nothing grows. Kinds (Ed, 2026-10-11, the small islands): only the playground; the sports grounds are left out of kinds.
_legendClearing: Each area's sleeping legend lies in a small circular clearing of its own (Ed, 2026-10-06), where no tree or decor stands: radius metres across from its middle (species: a radius for that legend, sized to fit it: half its sleeping width plus 4 m), a soft ring edge metres wide marking it on the ground, and the legend lying top x radius north of the middle (the circle's far side from the camera), the open floor in front. Quest sigils and relics take effect inside it. minFromStone (Ed, 2026-10-06: "The legend circle shouldn't spawn near its runestone"): its edge at least this many metres from its area's runestone (where the soundsystem comes), clear of the stone's clearing and the party's dance space; a small area with no such spot takes the farthest that fits (logged). minFromOtherStones (Ed, v1628: "Legend and runestone in the same place"): its edge at least this many metres from every neighbouring area's runestone too, always (not relaxed for a small area). floor (Ed, 2026-10-06: "The floor of the legend circle can be weathered and mossy stone with the legend's sigil carved into it. It's covered by moss etc and so you can't see it clearly"): on, old flagstones about slab metres across, the legend's sigil carved into them as dark grooves, overgrowth (0.5 as drawn, up to 1 for more) moss, grass and litter over them so the carving shows only in pieces; glint: how much the grooves catch the light while its legend sleeps (0, off: Ed's call later). rim: art builder 3's rim kit (#262) round its edge, a piece every spacing metres of it at chance, out metres past its radius and up to spread more (on its ring, never its floor), none on a path nor within gap degrees of due south (the way in). grove (Ed, 2026-10-06: "an area of the tallest trees around each legend circle"; "It should blend back smoothly into the rest of the forest around this area, so it doesn't stand out too much"): round the circle's ragged edge the forest swells, strongest at the edge and easing out (smoothstep) over reach metres to the area's own: there trees stand at up to density (a chance a tree spot), up to tallest of them the area's two tallest kinds, drawn up to scale times bigger, each tree's strength jittered by jitter either way so no ring or step shows; open in front, gap degrees either side of due south (toward the camera), easing in over soft degrees more, for the way in and the view of the legend.
_scenes: Scenes (Ed, 2026-10-04; art/scenes.js): small vignettes (a farmyard corner, a bus stop, a picnic gone wild...) and large landmarks (a cemetery, a car park, ruined churches and temples, castle ruins...), each a few pieces counting as one, each at most once per map. The legend and the circle baby are the exceptions"; and "they should lose interest and go home if you leave their area, as they did before"; rules/hunt.ts): once a wild area's watch is over with her on the ground in it, every one of its own awake young and adults hunts her while she's in the area, wherever in it they are, never giving up or napping; over the treetops there they hold and come on again when she lands. It ends for one when it's invited, enraged, or knocked down and run off; for all of an area's when she leaves the area (they're ordinary wild creatures again: they give up combat.leaveArea metres past their edge and walk home, as before); for all of hers when she's knocked out (they give up, walk home and roam, DECISION FOR ED, and the area's watch plays again on her next visit). Back in an area she left, it hunts her again at once while it's remembered (wildWatch.forget seconds after she was last on the ground in it), else its watch plays again. _guard: Parked party animals (at a sigil on the ground) guard it (Ed, 2026-10-04): they take on any wild creature of another kind within radius metres of the sigil, and come back to it. _creatures: Wild creatures (Ed, 2026-10-04): every area starts with the same population, population.start (one baby and one young: Ed, 2026-10-05, 'actually, the game should start with one baby and one youth, otherwise you can't avoid enraging lots of legends', after 'the game is hard! we should start each area with just one baby'; before it, one young and one adult, and before that one baby and two adults), and, from the start (Ed, 2026-10-07: his new core design, "no population growth on a clock"), more by its place on the waves' route (Balance 2's shape; rules/growth.ts routePopulation): byRoute.threat, [route index, F] points (1 the first wave's stone; straight lines between, flat past the ends), is the extra fighting value its young and adults add (F by Lanchester, young 11.6, adult 40, babies 0; about what an area woken at that wave grew to before); its kind spends it by its profile (byRoute.profiles[species], else default: the shares of its extra creatures as babies, young and adults), so many more of a swarm's young than of a heavy kind's adults, at the same danger: count = threat ÷ the profile's mean F a creature × the area's count scale, rounded, split by the shares (largest remainder, ties by the seed). byRoute.babies: babies in every area, start's included (Ed, 2026-10-07: about two, for quest sigils and berries), at most babyCap. byRoute.minHostile: at least this many young or adults in every wild area (Ed, 2026-10-07: "every wild area has at least one hostile wild creature"), any shortfall made up with young. The hostile swarm (Ed, 2026-10-08, the swarm plan's phase 1: its own young and adults, the ones a wave enrages and sets marching; rules/swarm.ts): its challenge grows with the area's place p in the runestone order (0 the first stone, 1 the last), whatever its species. swarm.classes: strong (cap 6), medium (cap 12: swarm.reference, and every species not listed) and light (cap 16; Ed: "a swarm of 20 is too many; cap it at 16"), each class's strength 12 / its cap on its creatures' health and damage (strong ×2, light ×0.75; rules/combat/data.ts), so moving a species is one line here. The target is the estimated power (Σhp × Σdps; the witch doesn't count: her three hits ignore damage) of a medium reference swarm of swarm.start + (swarm.endAverage − swarm.start)·p^swarm.curve creatures (1 + 11·p^1.3), its young share easing from swarm.youngShare[0] (1.0) to [1] (0.2). p is the master curve's (Ed, 2026-10-10, 2026-10-11): by the area's wave, (wave − 1)/(swarm.waves − 1), so wave swarm.waves (64) brings today's final swarm, every island plays it from wave 1 as far as it has areas, and a bigger map holds there after. Each area fields, of every size up to its species' cap (capScales: the cap grown along the same curve, at least 2) and every young/adult split, the one nearest the target; among those within swarm.mixTolerance (10%) of the nearest, a mix of young and adults first. A simulated power (config/swarm-power.json, empty in phase 1) stands in for the estimate where it has the swarm. So a default map (about 100 areas) holds about 540 hostiles: the curve's average, 5.8 an area. growth is the old growth on a clock, which the game no longer reads (the balance simulators still do): every wave, each area the party hasn't reached gained growth.perWave more (a fraction carries over: 0.5 is one every other wave; balance, 2026-10-06, DECISION FOR ED: 0.5, from 1, so a player's defence can hold the early sieges and playing well matters), each at a random level by growth.weights (baby, young, adult: equal thirds), so the areas the party reaches late are the ones to fear. Areas already partified don't grow. New ones arrive out of the witch's sight (beyond the haze's far edge plus growth.hide metres), never popping in on screen; areas far from every witch keep them as counts only, made real (from the seed) when a witch comes within creatureSimRadius of the area or it wakes. The home area holds none. Fighting value (DESIGN.md, Balance): a young is worth 15.5, an adult 29, a legend 76; so an area woken at wave n brings about 1 + n/3 young and 1 + n/3 adults (F about 44.5 + 14.8 n), besides its legend (wildLegends). Only creatures whose home is within creatureSimRadius metres of the witch move. node tools/balance/sim.mjs forecasts the sieges these numbers make.

__party: The party: the beat, waves, soundsystems, the dancefloor, its lights and objects, the party witches, the ley lines, music and sound, and the end.
_beat: The music's clock (beats per minute): the lasers sweep to it and party animals dance to it. Later the music itself drives it.
_lasers: Each playing soundsystem's laser show: bursts of blockBars bars, on about duty of the time (seeded per soundsystem), up to maxCount beams stepping on the bars, fanned over spread degrees (no beam tilting more than maxTilt from straight up), swinging sweep degrees once every sweepBeats beats (slow, like searchlights), opening and closing the fan every openBars bars, length metres tall, opacity 0-1, fading in over fadeIn and out over fadeOut seconds, and fading with distance from fadeNear to fadeFar metres. Glow only: no light, nothing from the light budget.
_speakerLasers: The dancefloor ring's lasers (Ed, 2026-10-04: none from the disco ball; one on top of each ring speaker): a single beam from each playing speaker, at most tilt degrees off straight up and leaning outwards, swinging sweep degrees sideways, over sweepBeats beats, neighbours out of phase; length metres, at opacity (thinner-looking than the area soundsystems' fans).
